messages.text: Ferrari vow to come back stronger after Monza 'failure'

metadata.summary: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says his team will head to this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid with "all the energy" to bounce back from their "failure" at Monza.
metadata.content: Spanish GP: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says team will come back stronger in Madrid after Italian GP 'failure' at Monza | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Spanish GP: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says team will come back stronger in Madrid after Italian GP 'failure' at Monza Ferrari scored just eight points last time out in Monza on a weekend they hoped Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc could fight for the win; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Tuesday 8 September 2026 11:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch back the 360-degree angle of Ferrari's Charles Leclerc's crash at the Italian Grand Prix Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says his team will head to this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid with "all the energy" to bounce back from their "failure" at Monza. There were big expectations for Ferrari at their home event after Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were quick in Friday practice, only to miss out on the front row in qualifying before a dismal race on Sunday. Hamilton dropped from fourth to 10th after going side by side with Leclerc at the first chicane, going through the gravel at Turn 2, which he was unhappy with. metadata.summary: Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister is "very sad" that he has not been offered a new contract and admitted he had "options to leave" in the summer.
metadata.content: Alexis Mac Allister: Liverpool midfielder 'very sad' over no new contract and admits he could have left in summer | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Alexis Mac Allister: Liverpool midfielder 'very sad' over no new contract and admits he could have left in summer Alexis Mac Allister 'very sad' at not being offered new Liverpool contract; 27-year-old midfielder has two years left on Anfield deal; team-mates Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch signed new long-term contracts this year Tuesday 8 September 2026 14:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexis Mac Allister opens up about his disappointment in not receiving a new Liverpool contract, but insists he is going to continue to give 100 per cent for the club Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister is "very sad" that he has not been offered a new contract and admitted he had "options to leave" in the summer. The 27-year-old confirmed he has two years left on his Reds deal, which he signed when he joined the club in the summer of 2023. The Argentina international's unhappiness comes after fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch penned new long-term contracts this year. Speaking ahead of Liverpool's Champions League opener against Atletico Madrid, Mac Allister told a pre-match press conference: "There was a chance [he could have left the club in the summer]. Howe's shock resignation in July led to the swift appointment of Matthias Jaissle , who has enjoyed an unbeaten start to his reign. Howe's exit was part of a turbulent summer for the Magpies which also included the departures of key players Bruno Guimaraes , Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon . metadata.content: Riccardo Calafiori: How Arsenal's defender has emerged as one of the Premier League's best left-backs | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Riccardo Calafiori: How Arsenal's defender has emerged as one of the Premier League's best left-backs Riccardo Calafiori has been called "the best left-back in the Premier League by far" by Jamie Carragher; the Italian has started the season with a goal in the Community Shield and two assists against Coventry and Aston Villa; Sky Sports' Sam Blitz analyses Calafiori's wild positioning Sam Blitz Football Journalist @SamBIitz Monday 7 September 2026 14:01, UK Image: Riccardo Calafiori has become a crucial cog in the Arsenal attack - as well as being a top defender Riccardo Calafiori returns to Italy with Arsenal this week - and he's a very different player compared to the one who departed for England two years ago. When Arsenal came in for Calafiori, he was regularly playing at centre-back at Bologna. Those who guided his career had doubts about whether he could reach the highest level as a left-back. metadata.summary: Jumps action from Bangor-on-Dee features live on Sky Sports Racing on Tuesday.
metadata.content: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Jumps action from Bangor-on-Dee features live on Tuesday | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Today on Sky Sports Racing: Jumps action from Bangor-on-Dee features live on Tuesday A Grade Two scorer over hurdles back in 2024, Roadlesstravelled looks to regain the winning thread on his chase debut at Bangor-on-Dee; we have six races in all, live on Sky Sports Racing from 4.38pm Monday 7 September 2026 10:44, UK Image: Bangor is the venue for Sky Sports Racing's live action on Tuesday Jumps action from Bangor-on-Dee features live on Sky Sports Racing on Tuesday. 5.12 Bangor-on-Dee - Roadlesstravelled makes chase debut Grade Two winner Roadlesstravelled makes his chase debut in the John Hewitt Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase . The seven-year-old began his career impeccably, winning three from three over hurdles, including a Grade Two novice hurdle. He has regressed markedly since, pulling up in the Formby Novices' Hurdle in December 2024, and has spent some time on the Flat since. He ran too keen on his last Flat start and returns to obstacles to make his chase debut off nearly a four-month break. He won an Irish point-to-point quite takingly back in May 2023, so if Jonjo and AJ O'Neill have got him back in decent shape, he could run a solid race. messages.text: USA hold off epic Europe comeback to edge Junior Solheim Cup thriller

metadata.summary: Team USA held off a remarkable final-day fightback from Team Europe to successfully retain the Junior Solheim Cup with a narrow 13-11 win in the Netherlands.
metadata.content: Junior Solheim Cup: Team Europe produce epic singles comeback before Team USA close out 13-11 win at Bernardus Golf | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Junior Solheim Cup: Team Europe produce epic singles comeback before Team USA close out 13-11 win at Bernardus Golf Team Europe won 8.5 points on the final day but fell to a narrow home defeat against Team USA; Anne van Dam's European team briefly threatened the biggest comeback in the event's history; watch the Solheim Cup live on Friday from 6am on Sky Sports Golf By Ali Stafford at Bernardus Golf Tuesday 8 September 2026 15:32, UK Image: Team USA claimed a 13-11 victory at the Junior Solheim Cup Team USA held off a remarkable final-day fightback from Team Europe to successfully retain the Junior Solheim Cup with a narrow 13-11 win in the Netherlands. Morgan Pressel's side had dominated the opening day to take a seven-point lead into Tuesday's singles at Bernardus Golf, leaving them requiring only 2.5 points to retain the trophy and three for outright victory. The target required was the same Team Europe experienced during last year's Ryder Cup before they clung on to victory, although the visitors were left sweating as Anne van Dam's European side threatened a record-breaking comeback. messages.text: Rybakina too strong for Osaka as Zheng stuns Swiatek at US Open

metadata.summary: Elena Rybakina cruised into the US Open quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Naomi Osaka to keep her push for the world No 1 ranking on track.
metadata.content: US Open 2026: Elena Rybakina too strong for Naomi Osaka as Qinwen Zheng comeback stuns Iga Swiatek | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open 2026: Elena Rybakina too strong for Naomi Osaka as Qinwen Zheng comeback stuns Iga Swiatek Elena Rybakina beats Naomi Osaka in 66 minutes to set up a quarter-final against Qinwen Zheng, who mounted a stunning comeback to beat Iga Swiatek; Mirra Andreeva also into last eight with win over Anastasia Potapova; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis Tuesday 8 September 2026 11:18, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Naomi Osaka's match against Elena Rybakina at the US Open Elena Rybakina cruised into the US Open quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Naomi Osaka to keep her push for the world No 1 ranking on track. Rybakina will reclaim the top spot if she reaches the semi-finals, and after dismantling two-time champion Osaka on Louis Armstrong, she has every reason to believe she can go all the way and lift the US Open trophy. It took the second seed just over 20 minutes to wrap up the first set 6-1 before securing a decisive break midway through the second to quell a resurgent Osaka and seal an emphatic 6-1 6-4 victory.
